Rule 1.title: Application
Rule 1.summary: These Rules apply to all vessels on high seas (International) and inland waters (Inland). Special rules for roadsteads, harbors, rivers may be made by appropriate authority. Vessels 12m+ must carry a copy of these Rules.

Rule 2.title: Responsibility
Rule 2.summary: Nothing in these Rules exonerates any vessel from neglect of these Rules or neglect of ordinary seamanship. Due regard shall be had to all dangers of navigation and special circumstances which may require departure from these Rules to avoid immediate danger.

Rule 3.title: General Definitions
Rule 3.summary: Defines key terms: vessel, power-driven vessel, sailing vessel, vessel engaged in fishing, vessel not under command, vessel restricted in ability to maneuver, vessel constrained by draft, underway, length, breadth, in sight, restricted visibility, WIG craft, Western Rivers, Great Lakes, Inland Waters.

Rule 4.title: Application (Steering and Sailing Rules)
Rule 4.summary: Rules 4-10 apply in any condition of visibility.

Rule 5.title: Look-out
Rule 5.summary: Every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision.

Rule 6.title: Safe Speed
Rule 6.summary: Every vessel shall at all times proceed at a safe speed so she can take proper and effective action to avoid collision and be stopped within an appropriate distance. Factors include visibility, traffic density, maneuverability, background light, wind/sea/current, draft, and radar characteristics.

Rule 7.title: Risk of Collision
Rule 7.summary: Every vessel shall use all available means to determine if risk of collision exists. If any doubt, risk shall be deemed to exist. Compass bearing not appreciably changing indicates risk. Assumptions shall not be made on scanty information.

Rule 8.title: Action to Avoid Collision
Rule 8.summary: Action to avoid collision shall be positive, made in ample time, readily apparent. Alteration of course alone may be most effective if made in good time. Shall result in passing at a safe distance. May slacken speed, stop, or reverse.

Rule 9.title: Narrow Channels
Rule 9.summary: Vessel in narrow channel shall keep to starboard side. Vessels under 20m and sailing vessels shall not impede vessels that can only navigate within the channel. Fishing vessels shall not impede passage. Special rules for overtaking in channels. Sound signal near bends. Avoid anchoring in channels. On Western Rivers/Great Lakes, downbound vessel with current has right-of-way.

Rule 10.title: Traffic Separation Schemes
Rule 10.summary: Vessels using traffic separation schemes shall proceed in appropriate lane, keep clear of separation line/zone, join/leave at termination or at small angle. Cross at right angles. Vessels under 20m and sailing vessels shall not impede power-driven vessels in traffic lanes.

Rule 11.title: Application (Vessels in Sight)
Rule 11.summary: Rules 11-18 apply to vessels in sight of one another.

Rule 12.title: Sailing Vessels
Rule 12.summary: When two sailing vessels approach with risk of collision: wind on different sides, port-tack vessel keeps clear. Wind on same side, windward vessel keeps clear. Port-tack vessel seeing windward vessel and unsure of wind side shall keep clear. Windward side is opposite the mainsail.

Rule 13.title: Overtaking
Rule 13.summary: Any vessel overtaking another shall keep out of the way. Overtaking means coming up from more than 22.5 degrees abaft the beam (can only see sternlight at night). When in doubt, assume overtaking. Subsequent bearing changes do not relieve the overtaking vessel.

Rule 14.title: Head-on Situation
Rule 14.summary: When two power-driven vessels meet head-on, each shall alter course to starboard to pass port to port. Situation exists when masthead lights are in line and/or both sidelights visible. When in doubt, assume head-on. On Western Rivers/Great Lakes, downbound vessel has right-of-way.

Rule 15.title: Crossing Situation
Rule 15.summary: When two power-driven vessels cross with risk of collision, the vessel with the other on her starboard side shall keep out of the way and avoid crossing ahead. On Western Rivers/Great Lakes, vessel crossing a river keeps out of way of vessel ascending/descending.

Rule 16.title: Action by Give-way Vessel
Rule 16.summary: The give-way vessel shall take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

Rule 17.title: Action by Stand-on Vessel
Rule 17.summary: The stand-on vessel shall maintain course and speed. May take action to avoid collision when apparent the give-way vessel is not acting. Shall take action when collision cannot be avoided by give-way vessel alone. Shall not alter course to port for vessel on port side.

Rule 18.title: Responsibilities Between Vessels
Rule 18.summary: Hierarchy of vessel privileges: Power-driven keeps clear of NUC, RAM, fishing, sailing. Sailing keeps clear of NUC, RAM, fishing. Fishing keeps clear of NUC, RAM. Constrained by draft vessels have special consideration (International only). Seaplanes keep clear of all.

Rule 19.title: Conduct of Vessels in Restricted Visibility
Rule 19.summary: Applies to vessels not in sight of one another in restricted visibility. Proceed at safe speed, engines ready. Vessel detecting another by radar alone shall determine if close-quarters developing. Avoid alteration to port for vessel forward of beam. Hearing fog signal forward of beam, reduce speed to minimum.

Rule 20.title: Application (Lights and Shapes)
Rule 20.summary: Rules 20-31 apply in all weathers. Lights from sunset to sunrise. Shapes by day. Lights in restricted visibility. No other lights that could be mistaken for prescribed lights.

Rule 21.title: Definitions (Lights)
Rule 21.summary: Defines masthead light (225 degrees white, forward), sidelights (112.5 degrees, green starboard/red port), sternlight (135 degrees white, aft), towing light (yellow, same as stern), all-round light (360 degrees), flashing light (120+ flashes/min), special flashing light (Inland: yellow, 50-70 flashes/min, 180-225 degrees).

Rule 22.title: Visibility of Lights
Rule 22.summary: Minimum visibility ranges for lights: 50m+ vessels masthead 6nm, sidelight 3nm, sternlight 3nm, towing 3nm. 12-50m vessels masthead 5nm (3nm if under 20m), sidelight 2nm. Under 12m masthead 2nm, sidelight 1nm.

Rule 23.title: Power-driven Vessels Underway
Rule 23.summary: Power-driven vessel underway shows masthead light forward, second masthead light abaft and higher (50m+), sidelights, sternlight. Vessels under 50m not obliged to show second masthead. Under 12m may show all-round white and sidelights instead. Under 7m and under 7 knots may show all-round white.

Rule 24.title: Towing and Pushing
Rule 24.summary: Towing vessel shows two masthead lights forward if tow under 200m, three if over 200m. Also sidelights, sternlight, and towing light. Tow over 200m shows diamond shape by day. Pushed vessel shows sidelights forward. Inland: special flashing light on pushed ahead or alongside composite.

Rule 25.title: Sailing Vessels Underway and Vessels Under Oars
Rule 25.summary: Sailing vessel shows sidelights and sternlight. May show red over green all-round at masthead. Under 20m may combine in one lantern. Under 7m shall show white light or have ready a torch/lantern. Vessel under oars may show lights of sailing vessel or white light.

Rule 26.title: Fishing Vessels
Rule 26.summary: Trawling: green over white all-round lights, shape of two cones. Other fishing: red over white all-round, shape of two cones. Making way also shows sidelights and sternlight. Gear extending over 150m shows cone pointing in direction of gear. Under 20m may show basket instead of shapes.

Rule 27.title: Vessels Not Under Command or Restricted in Ability to Maneuver
Rule 27.summary: NUC: two red all-round lights vertical, two balls. RAM: red-white-red vertical all-round, ball-diamond-ball. Dredging: red-white-red plus red-red on obstructed side, green-green on clear side. Mining: three green all-round vertical. Under 12m NUC/RAM not required to show these lights.

Rule 28.title: Vessels Constrained by Their Draft
Rule 28.summary: International only: may show three red all-round lights vertical, or a cylinder shape by day, in addition to lights for power-driven vessel.

Rule 29.title: Pilot Vessels
Rule 29.summary: Pilot vessel on duty shows white over red all-round at masthead, plus sidelights and sternlight when underway. At anchor shows pilot lights plus anchor light. Pilot vessel not on duty shows normal vessel lights.

Rule 30.title: Anchored Vessels and Vessels Aground
Rule 30.summary: Anchored vessel shows all-round white forward and aft (aft lower). 50m+ also illuminates decks. Under 50m may show one all-round white. Under 7m not required if not in/near narrow channel or anchorage. Aground shows anchor lights plus two red all-round vertical. Inland: barges at special anchorage need only one all-round white.

Rule 31.title: Seaplanes
Rule 31.summary: Seaplanes unable to show lights/shapes of exact characteristics shall show lights/shapes as closely similar as possible.

Rule 32.title: Definitions (Sound Signals)
Rule 32.summary: Defines whistle, short blast (about 1 second), prolonged blast (4 to 6 seconds).

Rule 33.title: Equipment for Sound Signals
Rule 33.summary: Vessels 12m+ shall carry whistle, 20m+ also bell, 100m+ also gong. Under 12m not obliged but must have some means of making efficient signal. Bell/gong may be replaced by equivalent.

Rule 34.title: Maneuvering and Warning Signals
Rule 34.summary: International: One short blast = altering to starboard, two = port, three = operating astern. Inland: One blast = intend to pass on port side (leave to port), two blasts = intend to pass on starboard side. Doubt/danger signal: five or more rapid blasts. Bend signal: one prolonged blast. Overtaking signals in channels.

Rule 35.title: Sound Signals in Restricted Visibility
Rule 35.summary: Power-driven making way: one prolonged every 2 min. Underway not making way: two prolonged every 2 min. NUC, RAM, constrained by draft, sailing, fishing, towing: one prolonged two short every 2 min. Last towed vessel (if manned): one prolonged three short. Anchored: bell 5 sec every minute. 100m+ also gong aft. Aground: bell plus 3 distinct strokes before and after. Pilot vessel: four short blasts as identity signal.

Rule 36.title: Signals to Attract Attention
Rule 36.summary: Any vessel may make light or sound signals to attract attention, provided they cannot be mistaken for any signal authorized elsewhere in these Rules. Shall not use high-intensity lights (strobe) to impair lookout.

Rule 37.title: Distress Signals
Rule 37.summary: Vessel in distress and requiring assistance shall use signals described in Annex IV. Distress signals include: gun fired at intervals, continuous sounding of fog signal, rockets/shells with red stars, SOS, Mayday, orange smoke, flames, EPIRB, red flares.

Rule 38.title: Exemptions
Rule 38.summary: Vessels which comply with previous rules requirements are exempted from full compliance with new rules for specified time periods regarding light repositioning, characteristics, and additional lights.

Annex I.title: Positioning and Technical Details of Lights and Shapes
Annex I.summary: Detailed technical specifications for light positions, vertical/horizontal placement, spacing, screen angles, and shape dimensions. Includes minimum heights above hull, spacing between masthead lights, and intensity calculations.

Annex III.title: Technical Details of Sound Signal Appliances
Annex III.summary: Specifications for whistles including frequency ranges, audibility ranges, directional properties, and bell/gong specifications.

Annex IV.title: Distress Signals
Annex IV.summary: Lists all recognized distress signals: gun, continuous sounding, rockets with red stars, SOS, Mayday by radio, NC flags, square flag over ball, flames, red rocket/flare, orange smoke, arm signals, EPIRB, approved signals.

Annex V.title: Pilot Rules (Inland Only)
Annex V.summary: Law enforcement vessels may display flashing blue light. Public safety vessels may display alternating red and yellow light. Vessel Traffic Service regulations. Western Rivers considerations.
